School & learning

index noun

a list at the back of a book

also indexes, indices, table of contents, contents

classical

Quint. 10.1.57: indicem certē ex bibliothēcā sūmptum (Lewis & Short)
Plin. Ep. 3.5.2: fungar indicis partibus
M-O s.v. parts: index

index, indicis m.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

a list, catalogue, table of contents

A list of contents is classical (Quintilian, Seneca, Pliny); the alphabetical index at the back of a book is modern, and Morgan–Owens gives index rērum for it. The word’s other senses: a pointer, the forefinger (digitus index), an informer, a book’s title (see title, of a book).

Other words

  • index rērum (et verbōrum) — an index of subjects (and words)

    also used · modern · M-O s.v. parts: index (Rabikauskas; Hase)

Examples

  • Fungar indicis partibus, atque etiam quō sint ōrdine scrīptī nōtum tibi faciam.

    I’ll play the part of an index, and tell you too in what order they were written.Plin. Ep. 3.5.2

  • Quaere in indice.

    Look in the index.composed

See also book, title, page.
